title: Optimized Mononuclear Cell Isolation from Liver and Tumor Tissue
author: Chauhan, Feldbrügge, et al.
materials: Gibco Recovery Cell Culture Freezing Medium

Decontaminate the working space and equipment inside the biosafety cabinet using 70% ethanol to maintain sterility and prevent contamination. Pre-cool the centrifuge to 4°C and preheat the water bath to 37°C.1.Tissue storage preparation.a.Transfer cold MACS tissue storage solution into a 50 mL tube, ensuring the amount used can fully submerge the tissue sample. Immediately transfer the tissue into the solution post-surgery.Storage conditions: Store and maintain MACS tissue storage solution at 4°C until product expiry.Note: Ensure the tissue stays fully submerged to prevent dryness and necrosis.Note: If tissue delivery is delayed and same-day tissue processing is not feasible, place the tissue in the tissue storage solution and store it at 4°C for up to 12–14 h. Process the tissue the following day.b.Weigh the tissue first and NOTE down the weight of non-tumoral and tumor tissue section in the biosafety cabinet.2.Prepare Percoll stock solution.a.Prepare a 33% Percoll gradient medium by mixing 33% (v/v) Percoll solution with 67% (v/v) RPMI medium (without FCS). Mix thoroughly to ensure homogeneity and keep the solution at 20°C–25°C until use.

Storage conditions: Prepare the Percoll stock solution and store it at 20°C–25°C for same-day use only.Note: Prepare 30 mL of 33% Percoll solution for each gram of tissue. Begin by weighing the tissue to determine the necessary volume of 33% Percoll solution.Note: Prepare the 33% Percoll solution fresh on the day of isolation and keep it at 20°C–25°C until use.3.Thawing and transferring cell culture reagents.a.Thaw DNase I, Collagenase IV, to reach 20°C–25°C (Only Protocol 2).b.Thaw Gibco Recovery Cell Culture Freezing Medium.Storage conditions: Store and maintain it at 4°C until 24 hours. Protect from light.c.Transfer Percoll solution, RPMI (without FCS), RPMI + 10% FCS, PBS and RBC lysis buffer aliquots to 20°C–25°C (Storage conditions).CRITICAL: All time-consuming steps, such as preparing Percoll solutions thawing enzymes and media, setting PBS and reagents to 20°C–25°C or 4°C and pre-cooling the centrifuge should be completed in advance whenever possible. Preparing these steps before surgical sampling is essential, as the quality of results relies heavily on the rapid processing of resected liver cells post resection.

steps.title: Decontaminate workspace and pre‑condition equipment
steps.instruction: Wipe the biosafety cabinet and all equipment with 70 % ethanol, pre‑cool the centrifuge to 4 °C and pre‑heat the water bath to 37 °C.

steps.title: Prepare tissue storage and weigh samples
steps.instruction: Transfer cold MACS tissue storage solution into a 50 mL tube, fully submerge the resected tissue, keep the tube at 4 °C and store up to 12–14 h if processing is delayed; weigh each non‑tumoral and tumor section and record the weights.

steps.title: Prepare 33 % Percoll stock solution
steps.instruction: Mix 33 % (v/v) Percoll with 67 % (v/v) RPMI medium without FCS to make a 33 % Percoll solution; prepare 30 mL of this solution for each gram of tissue, keep at 20–25 °C and use the same day.

steps.title: Thaw enzymes and media, bring to room temperature
steps.instruction: Thaw DNase I and Collagenase IV (enzymatic protocol only) and bring them to 20–25 °C; thaw Gibco Recovery Cell Culture Freezing Medium, keep at 4 °C until use and protect from light; bring aliquots of Percoll, RPMI (no FCS), RPMI + 10 % FCS, PBS and RBC‑lysis buffer to 20–25 °C (or 4 °C where indicated).

steps.title: Power on TissueGrinder and incubator
steps.instruction: Switch on the TissueGrinder instrument (white light around all four corners), turn on the computer and log into the TissueGrinder software, then switch on the swinging‑rotor incubator and set it to 37 °C.

steps.title: Reconstitute Zombie NIR viability dye
steps.instruction: Bring the Zombie NIR Fixable Viability Kit to 20–25 °C, add 100 µL anhydrous DMSO to the lyophilized dye vial, mix until fully dissolved; store the kit at –20 °C, and after reconstitution use immediately or keep at –20 °C protected from light for up to one month.

steps.title: Add Percoll for mechanical digestion
steps.instruction: Add 30 mL of 33 % Percoll directly to the TissueGrinder (TG) tube containing the cell pellet from tumor and non‑tumor sections, transfer the suspension to a new 50 mL tube (due to weight and non‑sealing lid), and resuspend the pellet to a uniform suspension.

steps.title: Add Percoll for enzymatic digestion
steps.instruction: Add 30 mL of 33 % Percoll directly to the tube containing the cell pellet from tumor and non‑tumor sections, then briefly pipette to resuspend before centrifugation.

steps.title: Centrifuge cell suspension
steps.instruction: Spin the 50 mL tubes at 1000 × g for 20 min at 24 °C with acceleration set to 1 and brake set to 0; do not activate the brake.

steps.title: Aspirate supernatant gently
steps.instruction: Carefully aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the loosely suspended immune‑cell pellet at the bottom of the tube.

steps.title: RBC lysis
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL RBC lysis buffer, incubate 5 min at 20–25 °C; then add 10 mL cold PBS, pool all tumor‑section tubes together and all non‑tumor‑section tubes together into separate 50 mL tubes.

steps.title: First PBS wash
steps.instruction: Fill each tube to 50 mL with cold 1× PBS, centrifuge at 877 × g for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Second PBS wash
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant, resuspend each pellet in 50 mL cold 1× PBS, and centrifuge again at 877 × g for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Resuspend in FACS buffer
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant and resuspend the final pellet in 1 mL FACS buffer.

steps.title: Filter cell suspension
steps.instruction: Pass the cell suspension through a 40 µm cell strainer into a 15 mL tube using a pipette.

steps.title: Count viable cells
steps.instruction: Mix 10 µL of the cell suspension with 10 µL Trypan blue (1:1), load 10 µL of the mixture onto a Luna Cell Counter slide, and count cells according to the mononuclear‑cell protocol.

steps.title: Keep cells on ice
steps.instruction: Store the isolated immune cells at 4 °C until flow‑cytometry analysis.

steps.title: Prepare antibody master mix
steps.instruction: Combine the antibodies listed in Table 1 (Zombie NIR dye 1 µL, CD45‑APC/Fire‑8 10 µL, CD34‑FITC 1 µL, CD123‑FITC 1 µL, CD14‑FITC 1 µL, CD19‑FITC 1 µL, CD11c‑FITC 1 µL, FcεRIα‑FITC 1 µL, TCRαβ‑FITC 1 µL, TCRγδ‑FITC 1 µL, CD3‑BV570 1 µL, CD4‑BV650 1 µL, CD8a‑BV510 1 µL, CD16‑AF700 1 µL, CD56‑BV605 1 µL, CD94‑PE/Dazzle 594 1 µL, CD161‑BV785 1 µL, CD127‑BV711 1 µL) to a total volume of 34.5 µL; keep the master mix on ice at 4 °C and use the same day.

steps.title: Pellet cells and add FACS buffer
steps.instruction: Aliquot 0.5–2 × 10⁶ viable cells into FACS staining tubes, add FACS buffer to a total volume of 3 mL, and centrifuge at 877 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Fc‑block incubation
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 99 µL FACS buffer, add 1 µL Human TruStain FcX, mix, and incubate 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash after Fc‑block
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 877 × g for 5 min at 4 °C and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Add antibody master mix
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 65.5 µL FACS buffer, add 34.5 µL antibody master mix, pipette to mix.

steps.title: Incubate antibodies
steps.instruction: Incubate the stained cells for 20 min at 4 °C in the dark; protect from light.

steps.title: Wash post‑antibody staining
steps.instruction: Add FACS buffer to bring the volume to 3 mL, centrifuge at 877 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Stain viability with Zombie NIR
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 99 µL ice‑cold PBS, add 1 µL reconstituted Zombie NIR dye, incubate 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Final wash
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL cold FACS buffer, centrifuge at 877 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, then gently aspirate the supernatant.

steps.title: Final resuspension
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL FACS buffer, resuspend the cell pellet by pipetting, and store at 4 °C until acquisition.

steps.title: Acquire flow cytometry data
steps.instruction: Run the stained samples on an available flow cytometer.

steps.title: Analyze data with FlowJo
steps.instruction: Import the FCS files into FlowJo and analyze the data on the same day.
